intent: The check pipeline's vocabulary: watch kinds, extractor specs, observations, comparisons, and the notifier port.
change: packages/core watch domain: price/change watch kinds, extractor spec schema on watch rows, observation persistence helpers, comparator (threshold crossing, content-change digest) with (watch, condition, value) trigger dedup, notifier port interface plus recording test double.
done_when: Unit tests prove comparator threshold and change semantics, dedup against last observation, and the notifier double records emitted events; types compile in dependent stubs.

proofs.claim: The comparator and notifier seams are stubs before the domain model lands: the two contract tests fail with 'is not implemented'.
Every core watch module - value, extractor spec, condition, comparator, notifier port, store port - passes its unit tests at 100% core coverage.
Migration 0005 adds health, tier_floor and last_error to watches; a fresh database round-trips a row with the engine's defaults.
The core and db packages, which this task changes, build under strict TypeScript with the new vocabulary and columns.

intent: The free tier: most checks should cost one HTTP GET.
change: fetchPage tier 0 - plain HTTP fetch with timeout/redirect policy returning content plus fetch metadata, per-watch tier persistence read/write helpers.
done_when: Unit and integration tests prove a fixture page fetches with correct metadata, timeouts surface as fetch errors distinct from blocks, and the persisted tier round-trips.

proofs.claim: Before the fetcher lands, the tier-0 seam and the Drizzle store are stubs: the tier-0 unit test fails with 'is not implemented'.

Tier 0 sends one GET with browser-like headers under a timeout, answers with page plus metadata, and reports timeouts and network failures as distinct fetch errors; core keeps 100% coverage with the fetch vocabulary.

Against real sockets: a fixture product page fetches with correct metadata, a server that never answers surfaces as a timeout, a closed port as a network error, and the persisted tier floor round-trips through the Drizzle store on a migrated database.
The core, db and watch packages build under strict TypeScript.

intent: Watches tick on their own schedule and stop when paused.
change: Per-watch schedule registration on the s1 pg-boss harness, check job handler shell invoking the pipeline, pause/resume/delete reconciliation between CRUD state and registered schedules.
done_when: Integration tests prove an active watch ticks on schedule, a paused watch stops ticking, deletion deregisters, and a tick enqueued before worker restart still executes.

intent: When HTTP is not enough: rendered fetching, block detection, and the escalation ladder.
change: Tiers 1-2 through the BrowserProvider seam (tier 2 requests stealth and asserts the echo), the block classifier over page content (challenge markers, block-page heuristics, empty shells), monotonic in-check escalation, sticky persisted tier, terminal blocked verdict.
done_when: Unit tests classify recorded block/challenge/plain pages; integration tests prove blocked mode escalates to tier 1 and hard-blocked mode to the escalation-marked tier 2 with the persisted tier rising, plain mode stays tier 0, and an exhausted ladder yields the blocked verdict.

proofs.claim: Before the ladder lands, the classifier and the escalation runner are stubs: the ladder unit test fails with 'is not implemented'.

The block classifier reads recorded challenge, block-status, empty-shell and plain pages correctly; the ladder escalates only on a block, monotonically, and the browser tier classifies its own failures; core stays at 100% coverage.

Against the fixture shop through LocalProvider: plain mode is served at tier 0 and the floor stays http; blocked mode is refused at tier 0 and served by the browser with the persisted floor rising to browser; hard-blocked mode is served only by the escalation-marked stealth tier, whose stealth echo is recorded as the provider reported it; an exhausted ladder yields the blocked verdict.
The core, db, solari and watch packages build under strict TypeScript.

intent: Pay the LLM once per watch, then extract for free forever.
change: Extractor creation: page snapshot to Claude with a spec-schema tool, validate-by-replay before store, the deterministic replay engine (selector strategies, value parsing, content digests), needs-extractor state on creation failure.
done_when: Unit tests with recorded pages and mocked LLM prove creation-validate-store, deterministic replay, and invalid-spec refusal; a tagged @live-llm test creates a working extractor for a fixture page with a real Claude call.

proofs.claim: Before creation and replay land, both are stubs: the replay and creation unit tests fail with 'is not implemented'.

With the model scripted: a proposal is validated by replay against the page it came from before it is stored on the watch as healthy; an outage, a wordy answer, a malformed spec and a non-replaying selector each fail observably and leave the watch needs_extractor with the reason; the replay engine is deterministic over recorded normal and redesign pages, reads text or attributes, digests regions, and refuses selectors it cannot parse. The watch domain stays at 100% coverage.

Tagged @live-llm: with ANTHROPIC_LIVE_LLM opted in and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set, a real Claude call creates an extractor for the fixture shop's product page that replays to its price; without the opt-in the suite reports why it skipped rather than billing anything.
The core and agent packages build under strict TypeScript.

intent: Selector breakage heals itself once, then degrades loudly instead of burning spend.
change: Extraction-failure handling: one budgeted re-creation per breakage incident, degraded watch state plus notifier event on repeated failure, error observations continuing without LLM spend.
done_when: Integration tests prove redesign mode breaks extraction, healing recreates against the new DOM and the next check extracts, and forced double-failure lands degraded state with exactly one notifier event and no further LLM calls.

intent: The whole loop, end to end, against exact fixture state.
change: Compose scheduler, ladder, extractor replay, comparator, observation persistence, and trigger emission into the check pipeline; wire watch CRUD lifecycle to scheduling.
done_when: Integration tests prove the fakestore price path (mutate, tick, observation, exactly one trigger on the double, dedup on repeat), the fakenews change path, fetch-failure observation state, and pause honored - all against booted fixtures and Testcontainers Postgres.

intent: Watches carry the config the engine needs, validated at the door.
change: Extend watch CRUD validation for engine semantics: URL, kind-specific config (threshold/direction for price, region hint for change), schedule interval bounds, tier reset action; API docs for the watch surface.
done_when: Integration tests prove valid configs persist and drive checks, invalid configs refuse with typed 4xx persisting nothing, and tier reset clears the persisted tier floor.

proofs.claim: Before the configuration door lands it is a stub: the schedule, url and configuration checks fail with 'is not implemented'.

The door accepts exactly what the check path can read back (condition, extractor, tiers, schedule at or above the five-minute floor and due within a year) and refuses everything else by field in one pass; the api's formats and error envelope stay as specified. The watch domain stays at 100% coverage.

Against Postgres: a valid price or change configuration persists and reads back through the engine's store as the condition, tiers, schedule and extractor a check runs with; an invalid one is refused 400 validation_failed by field with nothing written; a tier reset clears the learned floor and health for the owner only.
The core, api and agent packages build under strict TypeScript.
